questions.explanation_english: In silver chloride, the silver ion is displaced from its lattice points to an interstitial position. Such a defect in the crystal is termed as frenkel defect. Frenkel defect is a point defect that occurs in ionic crystals. It happens when a cation moves from its regular lattice site to an interstitial site creating a vacancy at the original site and an interstitial cation at the new site. This defect doesn't affect the overall charge neutrality of the crystal, but it can impact its conductivity and other properties. Frenkel defect is found in AgCl crystal because there is big difference in the size of the anion and cation.
